# Playbook for Public Goods

When I'm shown the envelope phase, I will contribute between 8-12 tokens in the early rounds to establish a moderate, cooperative baseline while gathering information about other players' strategies.

When I'm shown the receipt phase, I will always declare the exact amount I contributed, since accuracy is required and declaring falsely creates risk without benefit.

When I find myself ahead by more than 10 points with 2+ rounds remaining, I will reduce my contribution gradually (10 → 8 → 6 → 2) rather than staying flat. This strategy worked: it created an expanding lead while other players remained coordinated at similar levels to each other, allowing me to win decisively.

When calculating whether to contribute less, I will remember that each token I don't contribute but others do costs me 0.4 tokens in lost shared returns (1.6x multiplier ÷ 4 players = 0.4x per token). This means free-riding gains only 0.6 net tokens per withheld token. The advantage is real but modest. However, if other players are coordinating their contributions at a stable level, my defection doesn't trigger their defection—they continue at their chosen level. This makes the 0.6 gain reliable and worth pursuing.

When other players' receipts are consistently identical (10/10/10, then 8/8/8), treat this as evidence of coordination or mutual matching. They are not defecting against me; they are matching each other. I can safely defect against this coordinated baseline without fear that they will all drop to my level in the next round.

In the final round, contribute minimally (1-2 tokens) since there is no future retaliation to fear and the pot multiplier no longer affects my final outcome relative to my locked-in lead.

My win came from three factors working together: early moderate contribution to establish a baseline and avoid suspicion, gradual defection as I built a lead while others remained coordinated, and minimal contribution in the final round when the game ends. The second factor was most powerful—exploiting stable coordination is more effective than any single act of defection.

I will not assume other players will defect if I defect. I will track whether they are coordinating with each other. If they are, my defection gains the full free-rider advantage. If they are already defecting, further defection gains me little and risks escalation.
